title: Proposal for a Regulation amending Regulation (EU) 2024/1787 on the reduction of methane emissions in the energy sector as regards the postponement of certain obligations, COM(2026) 569 final
key_claim: The Commission proposes to postpone by one year the importer equivalence duty and the methane-intensity duties; the first annual equivalence demonstration moves to 31 May 2029, intensity reporting to 5 August 2029 and the maximum-intensity test to 5 August 2031, with the 4 August 2024 contract cut-off unchanged, citing the Strait of Hormuz disruption since 27 February 2026.
frame_summary: The Commission treats the delay as a one-year timetable adjustment for importers and national authorities, leaving the scope of covered contracts as it was.
verbatim_quote: the contracts concluded or renewed on or after 4 August 2024 for the previous calendar year’s supply of crude oil, natural gas or coal produced outside the Union cover only crude oil, natural gas or coal that is subject to monitoring, reporting and verification measures applied at the level of the producer
verbatim_list: Regulation (EU) 2024/1787 also requires importers to demonstrate and report, as of 1 January 2027, that contracts concluded or renewed after 4 August 2024 for the supply of crude oil, natural gas or coal produced outside the Union are subject to monitoring, reporting and verification measures that are equivalent to those set out in the Regulation at the level of the producer.

The obligations set out in Articles 28 and 29 of the Regulation should be postponed by one year, allowing third countries, importers, Union producers and competent authorities of the Member States to be in a position to implement them fully and effectively.
By 31 May 2029 and every year thereafter, importers shall demonstrate, and report in accordance with Article 27(1)
By 5 August 2031 and by 31 May every year thereafter, Union producers and importers placing crude oil, natural gas and coal on the Union market

title: Global Methane Tracker 2026
key_claim: The methane tied to oil and gas imported by the EU, UK, Japan, Korea and China (15 Mt in 2024) is three times their domestic production (5 Mt), and import-side intensity averages about 1% for the EU and UK.
frame_summary: The IEA frames import-side methane as larger than domestic methane for the main importers, so import standards reach the larger share of emissions.
verbatim_quote: In the European Union, the United Kingdom, Japan, Korea, and China, the methane tied to imported oil and gas (15 Mt in 2024) dwarfs that from domestic production (5 Mt in 2024).
verbatim_list: More than 35 Mt could be avoided at no net cost, based on average energy prices in 2025.

The average upstream methane emissions intensity of oil and gas imports varies widely by country: based on IEA estimates, it is around 1.3% for China, 1% for the European Union and United Kingdom, and 0.6% for Japan and Korea.

title: European Parliament votes to approve three-year delay on EU methane rules
key_claim: Parliament backed a three-year delay on 22 October; importers would have until 31 May 2031 to show that contracts concluded or renewed since 4 August 2024 cover only equivalent-standard fuel; France, the US, Czechia and Italy had lobbied for three years.
frame_summary: Reports Parliament's vote as a longer delay than expected, driven by member-state and US lobbying.
verbatim_quote: Under Parliament's proposal, importers of crude oil, natural gas and coal would have until May 31, 2031, to show that supply contracts concluded or renewed since August 4, 2024 cover only fuel subject to monitoring, reporting and verification measures equivalent to EU rules,
verbatim_list: The rules, originally due to take effect on January 1, 2027, would have required foreign oil and gas suppliers to the EU to monitor and report methane, a potent greenhouse gas.
